subject: DPA - retention & deletion language / evidence follow-up
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@aureumhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Gallagher <tom.gallagher@procure-globe.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA redline: retention, residency, deletion evidence

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the redline we received last week (attached for reference). Our legal and security teams have a few open items around the retention and deletion sections that we need clarified before we can proceed to signature. High-level asks below: 

- Can Redwood confirm maximum retention for production data and debug logs (including tombstones) and whether those differ across regions (EU vs. US)?
- We need explicit language on how backup copies are handled after a deletion request — timeline and whether backups are included in the erase guarantee.
- Our auditors ask for a method to obtain proof-of-deletion (signed attestation + internal audit id) and an estimate for delivery lead time after a contract-triggered erase.

I attached a marked-up DPA for context (Aureum_DPA_redline_v1.docx). Can your team propose replacement wording for the redline items above — ideally two options: a conservative (enterprise) version and a practical (SaaS) version.

We'd like to resolve language this week to keep the procurement timeline. Available for a short call if helpful.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Legal Ops
Aureum Health

Attachments: Aureum_DPA_redline_v1.docx (docx)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@aureumhealth.com>
Cc: Tom Gallagher <tom.gallagher@procure-globe.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA redline: retention, residency, deletion evidence

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the context; we can absolutely propose two tracks. High-level responses first, then I included proposed language snippets below for you and legal to consider.

Quick answers:
- Production tokenized user data: default retention is 90 days for ephemeral traces; request-based erasure will remove primary copies within 5 business days (subject to the carveouts below).
- Debug/troubleshooting logs and tombstones: retained for 30 days by default; if longer retention is needed we can offer a tiered option (see practical vs conservative wording).
- Backups: our standard backups are retained for 30 days and included in the deletion workflow where technically feasible; due to backup replication windows there is a maximum final irrevocable purge window of 45 days after a deletion request in the conservative track.
- Proof-of-deletion: we can provide an attestation package that includes (a) internal deletion job id, (b) timestamped job logs, and (c) signed statement from Redwood operations. Delivery SLA: 10 business days for standard customers; enterprise customers can request 5 business days + prioritized ops review.

Proposed wording (two options) — please take these as starting points and we can refine to match your counsel's style:

Practical / SaaS option (recommended for typical production workloads):
"Upon receipt of a verified deletion request, Redwood will delete the Customer's primary copies of Customer Data within five (5) business days. Redwood's backup systems, which are used for service continuity and disaster recovery, will be removed in the next scheduled backup cycle and fully purged within forty-five (45) days of the deletion request. Redwood will provide a deletion report (containing job id, timestamps, and verification hashes where applicable) within ten (10) business days of request."

Conservative / Enterprise option (for stricter compliance postures):
"Upon receipt of a verified deletion request, Redwood will promptly commence deletion of Customer's primary copies of Customer Data. Copies maintained solely for backup and disaster recovery may be retained for up to forty-five (45) days to allow for replication and system integrity checks; Redwood will perform an irrevocable purge of such backup copies within forty-five (45) days of the deletion request unless otherwise agreed in writing. Redwood will deliver a signed deletion attestation, including internal job identifiers and associated logs, within five (5) business days of request."

Residency clarifications:
- We will honor region-scoped hosting commitments in Appendix A. If Customer requires onshore-only backups, that can be implemented via the Dedicated or Private deployment options and scoped in the DPA (additional fees may apply).

Next steps / asks from Aureum:
1) Which variant (practical vs conservative) does Aureum prefer?
2) Confirm whether backups must be onshore-only (EU) or if geo-redundant backups are acceptable.
3) Any special audit/attestation format required by your auditors?

I attached a short markup with inline edits (Aureum_response_markup.docx). Happy to jump on a 20-min sync with you + Tom to finalize.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Aureum_response_markup.docx (docx)

From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@aureumhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Gallagher <tom.gallagher@procure-globe.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA redline: retention, residency, deletion evidence

Soojin — thanks for the quick and thorough reply. A few clarifications from our side before we pick a variant:

- The auditors need any backup purge window to be no more than 30 calendar days for PHI-associated projects; can Redwood meet 30 days for the EU region if we select the Dedicated deployment?
- For the deletion attestation: we require evidence of removal from tertiary replicas as well (not just primary + backups). Can you confirm whether tertiary replicas are included in the attestation scope?
- Finally, our procurement team asked whether the 5 business day SLA for primary copy removal can be tightened to 3 business days for our enterprise tier (we are willing to include that in an SOW).

We're attaching a short summary of the security team's expectations for reference. If you can provide a one-sheet that maps your practical vs conservative wording to these items (30-day backup purge, tertiary replica scope, 3-day primary removal for enterprise), that will help speed review.

Appreciate it — Marta

Attachments: Aureum_requirements_summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@aureumhealth.com>, Tom Gallagher <tom.gallagher@procure-globe.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Aureum DPA: mapping ask + internal action items

Karthik, Marcus — forwarding the latest from Aureum (below). Key asks they want mapped to our proposed wording:

1) Backup purge window: they need 30 calendar days for PHI projects if we use Dedicated. Can we offer a dedicated-only commitment of 30 days (technical ops + legal both sign off)? If not, what's the minimum safe window for onshore-only backups across EU clusters?

2) Tertiary replicas: Marcus, please confirm whether us-east replicas or cross-region cold copies are covered by our deletion job and whether we can include tertiary replica deletion proof in the attestation package (job ids + logs). If there is a replication lag that prevents inclusion, state the exact window so I can propose it to Aureum.

3) SLA for primary removal: Karthik, they asked whether 3 business days for enterprise SOW is feasible. We need an ops cost estimate (priority queueing + manual verification + attestation) and whether we can automate the attestation generation to meet 3 days.

Deliverable for Aureum: a one-page mapping doc that shows (left) their ask and (right) our practical vs conservative responses, with explicit numbers for: primary removal SLA, backup purge window, tertiary replica coverage, attestation SLA. Target: EOD tomorrow.

I'll draft the one-pager once you send numbers. I'll also attach the evidence playbook outline as a starting template for the attestation contents.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
